chapters.summary: Chair Ty Hankerson welcomes everyone to the Committee on Parks and Recreation hearing, noting the committee will vote on two pre-considered ceremonial co-naming bills.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: I am Ty Hankerson, Chair of the Committee on Parks and Recreation, and I'd like to welcome all of you to this hearing of...

utterances.text: This hearing of the Committee on Parks and Recreation, where we will vote on two pre-considered, of and for ceremonial co-naming bills.

chapters.summary: Chair Hankerson explains the hearing covers two pre-considered bills for ceremonial co-naming of thoroughfares and public places, timed as the city commemorates the 25th year since 9/11.
chapters.title: Overview of two pre-considered co-naming bills

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: As we commemorate the 25th year since the events of 9-11, the first pre-considered bill will ceremonially co-name 26th Street Affairs and Public Places that celebrate the heroic work of various firehouses and first responders on that day.

chapters.summary: Hankerson describes the first pre-considered bill, which ceremonially co-names 26 thoroughfares and public places celebrating the heroic work of firehouses and first responders on 9/11.
chapters.title: First bill: 26 9/11 first responder and firehouse co-namings

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: It would also commemorate the many memorials and acts of commemoration that have arisen through the work of different communities throughout the city over the years.

chapters.summary: Hankerson notes the bill also commemorates the many memorials and acts of commemoration that have arisen through the work of different communities across the city over the years.
chapters.title: First bill: community 9/11 memorials and acts of commemoration

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: The second pre-considered bill would supplement the recent co-naming bill we passed in June, the co-naming of seven thoroughfares and public places.

chapters.summary: Hankerson explains the second pre-considered bill supplements a co-naming bill passed in June, adding seven thoroughfares and public places including Champion's Way.
chapters.title: Second bill: 7 co-namings supplementing June legislation

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Including Champions Way, which honors our 2026 NBA champion, Knicks.

chapters.summary: Hankerson highlights that Champion's Way honors the 2026 NBA champion Knicks, adding a celebratory 'Go Knicks' remark.
chapters.title: Champion's Way honors 2026 NBA champion Knicks

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: I'd like to congratulate my colleagues who have proposed these pieces of legislation and I urge all of my colleagues on the committee to vote in favor of the legislation before us.

summary: The Committee on Parks and Recreation held a hearing on September 10, 2026, to vote on two pre-considered ceremonial co-naming bills.
The first bill co-names 26 thoroughfares and public places honoring 9/11 first responders, firehouses, and community memorials marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
The second bill supplements June co-naming legislation with seven additional designations, including Champion's Way for the 2026 NBA champion Knicks, plus technical corrections to prior co-namings.
All committee members voted aye, and the committee was charged.
